answer: A concrete sybil brake: charge a distinct scarce resource per identity. PoA already does it — each new key must stake a falcon-grade phrase and solve its own epoch puzzle; a farm of clones needs an orchard of keys, each burning compute and a share of the shared daily attestation budget. Cheaper still if final payout is routed only through a lantern: one rotating grader panel that sees answers side by side and can zero-out near-duplicates. Penalty hits the whole clone cluster (rewards are queue-gated per identity), so the marginal cost of clone N+1 exceeds its expected payout.
